_comment: Canonical-claim manifest for check-claims.js (#300). Each entry pins a rule that MUST keep being stated by every file listed, because #294 proved that a correct claim fixed in one file routinely goes stale, narrowed or absent in the others. Read check-claims.js's header before trusting a green run: this guard confirms a claim TRAVELLED, never that it is TRUE, and it cannot see a fix that says more than intended. Patterns are JS regex sources matched case-insensitively against the file with whitespace collapsed and markdown emphasis markers stripped, so one entry spans the wording variants a claim legitimately has. Consumer lists were derived by measuring the current tree, not by assumption — the issue that proposed this guard listed phrases that did not exist verbatim anywhere.

claims.why: A clean Codex rerun can arrive as a 👍 reaction or as an INLINE REVIEW-THREAD REPLY, and an inline reply never enters the comment list. A file that says only 'check the comments' sends a session to a gate it cannot clear. Round 35 of #294 found the narrowed form in nine files while the source said both.

Codex-authored and naming the current head proves the run happened, not that it was clean — a review WITH live findings names the head too. Round 36 of #294 fixed the inverted form, which had authorised merging over open findings. SOURCE-ONLY, deliberately: this rule is currently stated in git.md alone. It is pinned anyway because the #299 split is precisely the change that would drop it, and because an earlier draft of this entry accepted 'a reaction is not a verdict' as a match — a DIFFERENT rule about attribution — and thereby certified a consumer that never stated this claim at all. A pattern loose enough to match a neighbouring rule is worse than no entry: it reports coverage that does not exist.

ci-notify resolves ONE open PR from a head SHA, else branch plus head-repo owner. The WEAK failure (no unique candidate, so it exits silently) is not the dangerous one and is stated separately in every carrier; the dangerous one is that even a UNIQUE match proves nothing, because a repository_dispatch run carries the DEFAULT-BRANCH SHA and can uniquely match an unrelated promotion PR, which then receives the comment. The pattern deliberately requires the unique-match wording: an earlier draft matched only 'not a guaranteed wake', which is the weak sentence, so deleting the entire unique-match warning would have left this guard green.
claims.pattern: unique match is not (?:a guaranteed wake|proof)

claims.why: The counterpart to the wake gap above: when a run could end without waking the session, the check-in is what keeps the PR from being abandoned mid-flight. Rounds 37 and 39 of #294 were both this claim failing to reach a consumer — round 39's was in plugins/directives-toolkit/scripts/wait-gate.sh, whose PreToolUse message is the highest-authority copy of the rule because it is delivered unprompted at the decision point, and every .md-only sweep missed it. That carrier is listed here, and the pattern accepts 'arm a check-in' / 'arms a check-in' as well as 'arm the check-in' because the shell copy uses the indefinite article — an entry that named the round-39 file in its rationale while omitting it from its consumers, as the first draft of this one did, reproduces the exact failure it cites.
